meta.title: Nike Has Never Owned a Single Shoe Factory
meta.hook: Nike has never owned a single factory that makes its shoes.
meta.description: Nike designs and markets its shoes but has never manufactured them itself. Per its own FY2024 filings, contract manufacturers ran 96 finished-goods footwear factories across 11 countries, with Vietnam alone producing about half of all Nike-brand footwear that year.

scenes.narration: Nike has never owned a single factory that makes its shoes.

visual.visual_intent: A single sneaker on a plain lit surface, product-style macro, clean
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the surprising negative fact

scenes.narration: Every pair is built by outside manufacturers Nike contracts with, not Nike itself.

visual.visual_intent: A footwear assembly line with workers assembling shoes, documentary realism, overhead angle

scenes.narration: As of Nike's own twenty twenty-four filings, contract manufacturers ran ninety-six footwear factories across eleven countries.

visual.visual_intent: A stylized world map with glowing nodes marking factory locations, dark background, clean data graphic
visual.decision_reason: exact figures from Nike FY2024 Form 10-K

scenes.narration: Vietnam alone made about half of all Nike footwear that year. Indonesia and China made most of the rest.

visual.visual_intent: A donut chart on a dark screen showing one dominant segment, clean financial graphic style
visual.decision_reason: Nike FY2024 10-K: Vietnam ~50%, Indonesia ~27%, China ~18% of footwear

scenes.narration: Nike's actual factory floor is a design studio, a marketing budget, and a spreadsheet of supplier contracts.

visual.visual_intent: A designer's desk with shoe sketches and material swatches, natural light, creative studio

scenes.narration: That's deliberate. Owning factories means owning fixed costs, labor risk, and capacity Nike can't easily undo.

visual.visual_intent: Heavy industrial machinery in a factory setting, cool light, wide shot
visual.decision_reason: explains the strategic rationale for outsourcing

scenes.narration: Contracting it out means Nike can shift production countries faster than it could ever build a new plant. Follow for more.

visual.visual_intent: Stacked shipping containers at a port, wide shot, cinematic golden light
visual.decision_reason: closing payoff on supply-chain flexibility, CTA
